title: SWE-1.5: THE SPEED ERA
lede: October 29, 2025. A frontier-size model — hundreds of billions of parameters — served at up to 950 tokens per second on Cerebras wafer-scale silicon. SWE-1.5's claim was not that it was the smartest model in the room; it was that the smartest model in the room had always been allowed to be slow, and that stopped here.
body:
## THE SPEED CLAIM
950 tok/s6×13×
peak serve ratefaster than haiku 4.5faster than sonnet 4.5
The stack was co-designed end-to-end — model, inference, and agent harness treated as one system. Serving came via a partnership with Cerebras, whose wafer-scale hardware runs the model at rates conventional GPU clusters don’t reach. The pitch to users was simple: you no longer choose between an AI that thinks fast and one that thinks well. ## THE FALCON ALPHA AFFAIR Before launch, the model beta-tested undercover. Windsurf users noticed a mysterious entry in the model picker labeled Falcon Alpha — an unannounced checkpoint collecting real-world telemetry. The annals record this as the moment the lab learned to dress its research in a trench coat. ## THE SUPPORTING CAST SWE-1.5 didn’t arrive alone. Two weeks earlier — October 16, 2025 — Cognition released SWE-grep, an agentic model trained purely for rapid context engineering: the retrieval specialist that finds the right code before the flagship reasons about it. The pattern of pairing a big thinker with a fast fetcher persists in the product to this day — see the invisible models exhibit. > Developers shouldn’t have to choose between an AI that thinks fast and one that thinks well. — Cognition, October 29, 2025 ## THE ARCHIVE NOTES * Availability: Windsurf model picker, all tiers. * Architecture: undisclosed; ‘frontier-size, hundreds of billions of parameters’ is the on-record figure. * Legacy: the speed bar it set (950 tok/s) became the default expectation — every later SWE release is measured against it. Next hall: same silicon, smoother manners — SWE-1.6.
